title: Generative AI Terrorism Risk Assessment Act
action: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs.
summary: The Generative AI Terrorism Risk Assessment Act proposes a framework for evaluating how generative AI could be used to plan or carry out terrorist acts. It requires developers and users to assess these risks, report them to authorities, and implement safeguards to prevent misuse.

title: Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026 is a piece of legislation designed to tackle the ecological footprint of AI technologies. It establishes standards and reporting requirements to ensure that the development, deployment, and operation of AI systems minimize their negative environmental effects.

title: Doctors Not AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on Ways and Means, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Doctors Not AI Act of 2026 is a law that prohibits artificial intelligence from providing medical care or making clinical decisions. It requires all diagnoses and treatments to be performed by licensed human doctors, with AI limited to supportive roles only.

title: Full AI Stack Export Promotion Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute by the Yeas and Nays: 37 - 7.
summary: The Full AI Stack Export Promotion Act aims to boost the U.S. competitiveness in artificial intelligence by encouraging the export of complete AI solutions—from hardware and software to data and services. It provides incentives, streamlined regulations, and support for companies that develop and ship integrated AI systems to global markets.

title: Open-Source AI Leadership Act
action: Forwarded by Subcommittee to Full Committee by Voice Vote.
summary: The Open-Source AI Leadership Act is a proposed law aimed at promoting the development and use of open‑source artificial intelligence technologies. It seeks to support collaboration, transparency, and innovation by encouraging government and industry to invest in and adopt open‑source AI frameworks.

title: Responsible Artificial Intelligence for Veterans Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The Responsible Artificial Intelligence for Veterans Act of 2026 proposes regulations to ensure that AI technologies used in veteran services are fair, transparent, and protect veterans' privacy. It aims to create oversight and accountability for AI systems that support healthcare, benefits, and other services for veterans.

title: Advanced AI Security Readiness Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select).
summary: The Advanced AI Security Readiness Act is a legislative proposal aimed at strengthening the security and resilience of AI systems. It focuses on establishing standards for AI development, deployment, and monitoring to mitigate risks and protect against potential threats.

title: Eliminating Bias in Algorithmic Systems Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.
summary: The Eliminating Bias in Algorithmic Systems Act of 2026 is intended to reduce discriminatory outcomes in AI by requiring developers to assess and mitigate bias in their systems. It creates a framework for audits, transparency, and accountability, including public reporting requirements and oversight by a government agency to ensure fair and equitable algorithmic decision-making.

title: Deterring American AI Model Theft Act of 2026
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 43 - 0.
summary: The Deterring American AI Model Theft Act of 2026 is a proposed law designed to protect American developers from having their AI models stolen or copied without permission. It establishes stricter penalties and enforcement mechanisms to deter unauthorized use and encourages secure practices for training and distributing AI systems.

title: Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025 requires companies that use automated decision‑making systems to assess and mitigate the risks of bias, discrimination, and other harms that their algorithms might cause. It also mandates transparency and public disclosure of how these algorithms operate and impact individuals and society.

title: Defense AI Reliability and Reporting Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Armed Services.
summary: The Defense AI Reliability and Reporting Act establishes standards to ensure the safety and effectiveness of artificial intelligence systems used by the U.S. Department of Defense. It requires detailed reporting on AI development, deployment, and performance to maintain transparency and accountability.

title: LIFT AI Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The LIFT AI Act is a proposed law that aims to regulate artificial intelligence so it remains safe, fair, and transparent for everyone. It establishes new standards, oversight, and accountability measures to protect privacy and prevent bias in AI systems.

title: China AI Power Report Act
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 47 - 0.
summary: China’s AI Power Report Act requires companies that build or use AI systems in China to submit regular reports on the amount of electricity their AI models consume and their energy efficiency. The law also sets national standards for reducing AI’s environmental impact and creates a regulatory framework to track and improve the sustainability of AI technologies.

title: Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on House Administration.
summary: The Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act is designed to safeguard the integrity of elections by restricting the use of artificial intelligence that can manipulate or mislead voters. It establishes regulations and penalties for creating or distributing deceptive AI content that could influence electoral outcomes.

title: Self-Improving AI Monitoring Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The Self-Improving AI Monitoring Act aims to set rules and oversight for artificial intelligences that can modify and enhance themselves without human input. It requires developers to report self-improving AI behavior, install safety checks, and give regulators transparency so the technology can be monitored for unintended consequences.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act proposes a temporary halt to the construction and operation of new AI data centers to address environmental and privacy concerns. It gives regulators time to develop guidelines and safeguards before allowing future AI data center projects to resume.

title: Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act
action: Ordered to be Reported by the Yeas and Nays: 44 - 0.
summary: The Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act is intended to shield households from the growing utility bills caused by the massive energy consumption of AI data centers. It proposes measures such as regulating data center energy use, encouraging renewable power, and offering financial relief to families whose electricity costs are impacted by AI infrastructure.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Act proposes a temporary pause on the construction of new data centers dedicated to artificial intelligence. It aims to address concerns about environmental impact, energy consumption, and regulatory oversight while stakeholders evaluate long‑term strategies.

title: LIFT AI Act
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 34 - 1.
summary: The LIFT AI Act is proposed federal legislation that aims to promote the safe and responsible use of artificial intelligence. It focuses on establishing standards for transparency, accountability, and public trust in AI systems.

title: Children's Artificial Intelligence Toy Safety Act of 2026
action: Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation. Ordered to be reported with an amendment in the nature of a substitute favorably.
summary: The Children's Artificial Intelligence Toy Safety Act of 2026 sets strict safety and privacy standards for AI-powered toys sold to children, requiring manufacturers to verify that the content and interactions are age‑appropriate and secure. It mandates testing, labeling, and enforcement measures to protect children from harmful or misleading AI behaviors.

title: Youth AI Privacy Act
action: Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation. Ordered to be reported with an amendment in the nature of a substitute favorably.
summary: The Youth AI Privacy Act is a proposed law designed to protect the personal data of children and young people when AI systems collect, analyze, or use their information. It sets strict rules for obtaining consent, ensures transparency, and mandates that companies implement robust safeguards to safeguard minors' privacy rights.

title: China AI Power Report Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Foreign Relations.
summary: The China AI Power Report Act requires the Chinese government to collect and disclose detailed information about the development, deployment, and impact of AI technologies in the country. The law aims to increase transparency, enable monitoring of AI progress and risks, and ensure accountability for AI-related decisions and applications.

title: READ AI Models Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The READ AI Models Act proposes regulations for the development and deployment of AI models to ensure transparency, accountability, and safety. It establishes standards for testing, documentation, and public oversight to protect users from potential harms.

title: A bill to provide for the delivery of artificial intelligence functional bills of materials, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Armed Services.
summary: The bill requires developers to produce a detailed “bill of materials” for each AI system, listing all hardware, software, data sources, and processes involved to improve transparency and traceability. It also sets out broader regulatory provisions for oversight, compliance, and responsible deployment of AI technologies.

title: Workforce for AI Trust Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The Workforce for AI Trust Act proposes establishing programs to develop a skilled workforce dedicated to building and overseeing trustworthy AI systems. It emphasizes training, certification, and incentives to ensure professionals can design, deploy, and maintain AI responsibly.

title: Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025 seeks to prevent companies from using artificial intelligence to inflate prices of AI services or manipulate labor market wages. It establishes regulatory standards for transparency, pricing fairness, and anti‑price‑gouging enforcement in AI‑driven industries.

title: FARM AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Agriculture.
summary: The FARM AI Act of 2026 establishes guidelines and safety standards for the use of artificial intelligence in agriculture, ensuring that AI tools used on farms are reliable, transparent, and respect farmers’ rights to data. It also requires farmers and agri‑tech companies to report AI performance, address potential bias, and comply with oversight to protect both the environment and consumers.

title: Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act
action: Placed on the Union Calendar, Calendar No. 619.
summary: The Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act is a legislative proposal designed to accelerate the development and deployment of AI technologies within banking, insurance, and investment sectors while safeguarding consumer interests. It establishes a regulatory framework that encourages innovation through incentives, sets clear standards for data privacy and algorithmic transparency, and creates oversight mechanisms to monitor AI‑driven financial products.

title: Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs.
summary: The Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act aims to boost the use of artificial intelligence in banking, investment, and other financial services by creating a supportive regulatory framework. It focuses on fostering innovation while ensuring consumer protection, data security, and compliance with financial industry standards.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Innovation Talent Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.
summary: This act aims to boost the development of artificial intelligence by supporting education, training, and hiring of AI talent, as well as encouraging innovation. It focuses on creating opportunities, incentives, and partnerships to grow a skilled workforce that can advance AI technologies.

title: No AI Data Centers on Federal Lands Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Natural Resources.
summary: The No AI Data Centers on Federal Lands Act would prohibit the establishment of AI data centers on federal property. It aims to protect federal lands from the environmental and operational impacts associated with large‑scale data processing facilities.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 18 - 15.
summary: The K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 requires schools to incorporate AI education into curricula to prepare students for a technology-driven world. It also mandates teacher training and equitable access to AI tools, ensuring all students gain foundational skills in AI concepts and responsible use.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions.
summary: The K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 is a federal law that requires schools to teach students about how artificial intelligence works and why it matters. It provides funding, training, and guidelines so teachers can add AI lessons to their curriculum and help students become responsible, informed users of technology.

title: CREATE AI Act of 2025
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 29 - 0.
summary: The CREATE AI Act of 2025 is a proposed law that sets rules for how AI systems can be designed, tested, and used. It focuses on protecting users, ensuring AI transparency, and creating oversight so that AI remains safe, accountable, and beneficial for society.

title: Understanding AI in the Classroom Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The Understanding AI in the Classroom Act seeks to ensure that teachers and students can effectively navigate and responsibly use artificial intelligence in educational settings. It outlines guidelines and resources for educators to integrate AI tools into curricula while safeguarding student privacy and fostering digital literacy.

title: Expressing the sense of the House of Representatives that every American and community impacted by the construction or operation of an artificial intelligence data center should have the right to transparency and local autonomy.
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on the Judiciary, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: Congress is saying that every person and community affected by the building or running of an AI data center should be able to see what's going on and have a say in how it impacts them. The bill aims to give people local control and clear information about these large tech facilities.
